correctness.rationale: Parseval reduces the joint two-parameter problem to one positive series after strict Fourier correlation alignment. Its derivative has sign G_t(a)-1, where G_t is strictly increasing because the exponential n-squared tilt decreases the baseline n-weighted mean, giving (log G_t)'≥tanh(a/2)>0. Endpoint limits yield a unique global minimizer, and evaluation at a=t yields strict first-moment bias. Uniform Riemann sums and Euler–Maclaurin establish the sharp small-time constants and the exactly canceled first correction; a convergent power series proves large-time coefficients. The 82 finite tests are ancillary, not infinite proofs.

originality.rationale: Bailey’s 2020-deposited thesis, Ch.6 Sec.6.3.2, previously writes exactly the same Fourier loss and stationary equation as a special case of fitting a wrapped-normal mixture with wrapped Cauchy. Those formulas are NOT asserted novel. The claim evaluated for originality is instead strict global uniqueness and strict first-moment bias at every heat time, plus explicit large-time and two-term singular short-time optimum laws. The inspected thesis calculates stationary roots numerically and does not provide those analytic extensions. Jones–Pewsey fixes first moments; statistical circular-kernel AMISE is a different optimization. The related accepted journal article remained inaccessible, so priority is best knowledge.

value.rationale: The conversion of one canonical diffusion multiplier family into another is a natural Fourier approximation problem with no arbitrary finite slice. The result determines the unique optimal Poisson time for every heat time, establishes a strict systematic bias relative to first-moment matching, and proves that the matched norm error is asymptotically t^{-1}, while optimal calibration achieves the provably sharp lower order J*/sqrt(t). The universal constant, exact short-time correction cancellation and explicit large-time coefficients make the fact useful as a precise analytic benchmark, not merely a computational exercise.
